transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you, too. Well, I came in today because... I keep having these thoughts lately. Just thinking that my family might be better off if I didn't wake up. It got bad enough that it really scared me, so I ended up telling my supervisor at work about it. And, well, that's what brings me here.
Have you thought about how you might kill yourself?
No, I haven't really thought about a specific way to do it. It's more just... a general feeling, you know? Just wishing I wouldn't wake up. I don't have a plan or anything like that.
Has anything particularly stressful or upsetting happened recently that you believe led to these thoughts?

Well, yeah, I suppose there is. My daughter recently left Georgia to go into the military. That was about two weeks ago. And... well, this whole change in me, it's been going on for about that long. Just since she left.
Since your daughter left, have you been feeling depressed or down most of the day, nearly every day?

I'm not really sure I'd call it depressed. I haven't really noticed feeling down all day long like that. It's just... well, I just have those thoughts I told you about. But I don't know that I'm walking around feeling sad the whole day, if that makes sense.
Since your daughter left, have you lost interest in or enjoyment of things you usually like to do?

Yeah, I have. I used to... well, I'd usually mess with my tomato plants, or go sand wood out at my bench. I'd watch the Falcons, or stay after church just talking to folks. But lately... I don't know. I just look at all that stuff like it belongs to somebody else. I haven't really wanted to do any of it.
Since your daughter left, how has your energy been? მ

I haven't really noticed any change in my energy, to be honest. I mean, I'm still getting up and moving around the same as always. I just... I don't feel like doing much of anything with that energy, I guess. But I wouldn't say I feel tired or drained or anything like that.
Since your daughter left, have you noticed any change in your sleep?
No, not really. I mean, I've been sleeping about the same as I always do. I go to bed and wake up at my usual times, so... no, nothing's really changed there.
Since your daughter left, have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty?

Yeah, I have. I just... I keep going over her leaving in my head, and I keep telling myself I must have failed her somehow. Like... well, like a better father would have done something different, you know? I just carry a lot of guilt about it.
Since your daughter left, have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions?

Yeah, I have. At work—I manage a distribution center—I'll just sit there and stare at the schedule or the routing sheet, and my mind just... it won't lock in. It's like I can't focus on it at all. And making decisions has been tough. Even little staffing calls feel way bigger than they ought to right now.
Since your daughter left, have you noticed any change in your appetite?

Yeah, it's dropped off a lot. Most days I really have to make myself eat even just a few bites. It's like... even the food I normally like, whether I'm at the warehouse or at home, it just sits there. I usually just end up throwing it out.
Since your daughter left, have these symptoms been present nearly every day?
Yeah, every day. It's been like this for about two weeks now... pretty much ever since she left Georgia to join the military. It just hasn't let up.
How much have these changes interfered with your ability to do your job or manage things at home?

It's... it's getting in the way a lot, honestly. At work, I started making mistakes, and they got serious enough that... well, a supervisor actually found me just sitting out in my truck before dawn one morning. Just sitting there. They ended up getting occupational health involved after that. 

And at home, it's not much better. I've just let the bills and my regular responsibilities pile up. I'm just not handling things the way I normally would.
Right now, do you feel you might act on these thoughts and try to harm yourself?

I don't think I'd actually do anything to hurt myself, no. But... well, that's really why I came in. I just keep having these thoughts that my family might be better off if I just didn't wake up. It scared me enough that I finally told my supervisor about it.
